quiz.title: Module 5 — Video Advertising
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers what makes an advertisement work: the hook, high-quality visuals, when the product appears, the problem-solution narrative, demonstration as proof, the metrics that measure creative performance, what a creative brief contains, and disclosure when using testimonials.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what is the most important element of a successful advertisement?
options: The background music.
The length of the advertisement.
The hook that captures the viewer's attention.
The number of products displayed.
questions.explanation: Everything after the opening depends on the viewer still being there. If the hook fails, the music, length and product count never get a chance to matter.

questions.prompt: Why should an advertisement have high-quality visuals?
options: To make the advertisement look visually appealing through good lighting, setting, and overall aesthetics.
To make the video look like a traditional television commercial.
To ensure that the advertisement is longer.
To reduce the need for a product demonstration.
questions.explanation: Lighting, setting and overall craft signal that the product is worth taking seriously. Production quality is part of the message, not decoration on top of it.

questions.prompt: According to the video, when should the product first become visible in an advertisement?
options: Within the first two seconds.
After the first 15 seconds.
Only during the final scene.
After the call to action.
questions.explanation: Viewers decide almost immediately whether the video is for them. Showing the product early tells them what they are watching before they scroll on.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a clear problem-solution narrative in an advertisement?
options: To entertain viewers without discussing the product.
To show the problem the audience faces and explain how the product solves it.
To list every feature of the product.
To focus only on the company's history.
questions.explanation: A problem the viewer recognises earns their attention, and the product arrives as the answer to it rather than as an unrelated pitch.

questions.prompt: Why is product demonstration important in an advertisement?
options: It makes the advertisement more complicated.
It replaces the need for a strong hook.
It provides proof that the product works and helps build consumer trust.
It allows the creator to avoid showing the product.
questions.explanation: A claim asks to be believed; a demonstration shows the thing working. Seeing it happen is what turns interest into trust.

questions.prompt: According to the video, which metrics are especially useful for evaluating creative performance?
options: Video resolution and number of followers.
Hook rate, hold rate, click-to-purchase ratio, spend, and return on ad spend.
Number of hashtags and comments only.
Cost per click and click-through rate only.
questions.explanation: These measure the journey the creative is built to drive — whether people stop, stay, and go on to buy — and whether the spend returned more than it cost.

questions.prompt: What should a creative strategist include in a creative brief?
options: Only the product name and price.
A general idea and leave the rest to the creator.
Scripts, storyboards, and shot lists to guide creators and editors.
Only the background music and video length.
questions.explanation: A brief that stops at a general idea leaves the editor guessing at the message. Scripts, storyboards and shot lists make the intent concrete enough to shoot and cut against.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what is important when using testimonials in advertisements?
options: Make the testimonial appear completely unscripted, even if it is misleading.
Remove all disclosures to make the advertisement look natural.
Include the appropriate FTC disclosure when there is a commercial connection between the testimonial and the brand.
Use trending copyrighted music to increase engagement.
questions.explanation: A paid or incentivised testimonial has to be disclosed. The audience needs to know about the commercial relationship to judge the claim fairly, and the disclosure is a legal requirement.
